summary: James Charles Colebrooke Sutherland worked in Indology and other fields. He studied at East India Company College and Fort William College under Thomas Roebuck, and served as professor of law at Presidency University.

James Darmesteter was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Michel Bréal (~1872–1877), later holding posts there (~1877–1894) and at the Collège de France (1885–1894).

James Duerlinger is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1964–1968) under Sheldon Pollock and held a post at the University of Iowa (~1971–2012).
James Dwight Dana studied at Yale College (~1830–1833) and held a post at Yale University (~1850–1892).

James Fergusson was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the Royal High School, Edinburgh, and became a member of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland in 1840.
James Fieser is a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied at Berea College and Purdue University (~1983–1986), and held a post at the University of Tennessee around 1992.
James G. Mullens is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at McMaster University and held a post at the University of Saskatchewan in 1989.
James Gibbs was active in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1870–1879) and President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1876–1881).

James H. Austin is a neurologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Nanrei Sohaku Kobori, Kyozan Joshu Sasaki, and Katsujo Terayama. He held posts at the University of Oregon, University of Colorado, and University of Idaho.

James Hadley was a linguistics and Indology scholar. He studied at Fairfield Academy and Yale College under Edward Elbridge Salisbury, later serving as professor of Greek at Yale University (1845–1872) and leading member of the American Oriental Society.

James Haughton Woods worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Harvard, the University of Strasbourg under Paul Deussen, and under Charles Rockwell Lanman, Arthur Venis, and Mukunda Shastri Adkar, later holding a post at Harvard in 1914.

James Irving Manatt worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Grinnell College and Yale under William Dwight Whitney, and held posts at Denison College, Marietta College, the University of Nebraska–Lincoln, and Brown University (~1892–1915).

James Ishmael Ford is a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure. He studied at Sonoma State University and Pacific School of Religion, training under Sojun Mel Weitsman, Jiyu-Kennett, and John Tarrant.

James Kenneth Powell II specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Northwestern University, the University of Chicago under David Tracy, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Isshi Yamada, and David M. Knipe.

James L. Fitzgerald is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under J. A. B. van Buitenen. He held posts as professor at the University of Tennessee (attested 2004–2006) and Das Professor of Sanskrit at Brown University (attested 2019).

James Legge was a sinologist who studied at Aberdeen Grammar School, the University of Aberdeen (~1831–1835), and Highbury College (~1836–1839). He was appointed professor at the University of Oxford in 1876.
James Luther Adams was a religious studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Minnesota, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University, where he later held a post (~1956–1968).

James Mackintosh was a scholar of history, archaeology, philosophy, and Indology. Educated at the University of Aberdeen and University of Edinburgh, he founded the Asiatic Society of Mumbai and served as its president (~1804–1811).

James Mallinson is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Eton, SOAS, and Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He held posts at SOAS (2013) and became Boden Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Oxford in 2023.

James Mark Shields is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. In 2016, he was attested as Associate Professor at Bucknell University and Overseas Collaborative Researcher at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies.
